title: IMF Press Release 25/072 — IMF and the Statistical Community Release New Global Standards for Macroeconomic Statistics (20 March 2025)
use: Dated release of BPM7 and distinction between publication and recommended country implementation; exact white-cover version scope.
verification: Opened and inspected the actual official release body: new seventh edition, English white-cover/pre-edited availability and recommended country implementation in 2029–2030. The manuscript does not assert that all datasets have implemented BPM7, or that the inspected pre-edited text is an unspecified final edition. No current macroeconomic observation is imported.

title: International Monetary Fund — Integrated Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Seventh Edition: March 2025 White Cover (Pre-Edited) Version
use: Resident external accounts, financial-account signs, statistical discrepancy, saving-current-account bridge, integrated IIP, valuation and residence reclassification; BPM7 terminology mapped to older BPM6 labels.
verification: Opened the actual 1,076-page PDF and inspected title/version, paragraphs 2.2–2.18 and 2.21–2.29 (printed pp. 12–21), 8.1–8.7 (pp. 307–309), 9.3–9.10 (pp. 323–327), residence-change paragraphs 9.37–9.39 (pp. 336–337), accrued-interest passages 7.28/7.44 and the Chapter 12 accrual/financial-counterpart example, 19.4–19.5 (pp. 609–610), and Tables A13.1/A13.2 (pp. 894–895). Actual body confirms earned/transfer income and statistical discrepancy replace the older primary/secondary income and net-errors-and-omissions terms. File URL contains bpm6 but its body is explicitly BPM7. An ashx variant failed; the linked PDF succeeded. Our numeric examples and their simplified timing are original. This is scoped inspection, not verification of the entire manual or of any country's adoption.

title: Stephanie Schmitt-Grohé, Martín Uribe and Michael Woodford — International Macroeconomics: A Modern Approach, Chapter 9 author slides: The Real Exchange Rate and Purchasing Power Parity (2022)
use: Method route for law of one price, real exchange-rate direction, absolute versus relative PPP and basket/price-index distinctions.
verification: Opened the actual 69-page author-hosted PDF and inspected the title, slides 2–5, 10–13 and 30–35 covering goods prices, home-currency-per-foreign quote, real rate, basket comparison and exact gross-growth expression before approximation. Read the warning that index levels can be normalized without changing their information. Chapter independently derives its own exact finite-growth and reciprocal-quote cases. No Big Mac data, country income comparisons or empirical PPP convergence claim is reproduced.

title: Stephanie Schmitt-Grohé, Martín Uribe and Michael Woodford — International Macroeconomics: A Modern Approach, Chapter 11 author slides: International Capital Market Integration (6 September 2022)
use: Covered investment and arbitrage paths, conditional expected uncovered returns and why free capital mobility alone does not imply UIP.
verification: Opened the actual 71-page author-hosted PDF; inspected slides 3–9 for complete financed covered-return comparison and 26–28 plus 31–42 for the asset-pricing setup, pricing-kernel conditions, CIP versus UIP and the covariance restriction. Chapter uses original numbers and proves elementary no-arbitrage cash flows; the full stochastic-discount-factor derivation is explicitly deferred. No historical capital-control statistics, regression coefficient or empirical causal effect from the slides is imported.

title: Claudio Borio, Robert McCauley, Patrick McGuire and Vladyslav Sushko — Covered interest parity lost: understanding the cross-currency basis (BIS Quarterly Review, September 2016)
use: Primary author discussion of executable covered positions, FX hedging, bid/ask and funding frictions, counterparty/liquidity risks and costly balance sheets.
verification: Opened the actual article (the legacy PDF URL redirected to its complete official HTML). Read the framework and Box A, plus the sections on limits to arbitrage, balance-sheet costs and empirical-proxy limitations. Quote convention is dollar/home currency per foreign unit. The chapter derives its own bid/ask inequalities and numerical cash flows; it imports no historical basis estimates, asserts no current spread, and does not treat the paper's proxy associations as a universal identified mechanism.
